batch_note: Yes, two templates repeat. (1) The 12 four-group/2x2 hypothesis items (A-01..03, B-01..03, C-01..03, D-01..03) all use the same option cast: one confounded diagonal (both-factor group vs neither-factor group, predicted by both accounts), one or two single-factor contrasts favouring the wrong side, and a key that is either the single-factor contrast isolating the target variable against the rival held constant (support) or the crossed pair of the two one-factor-only groups with the rival's group winning (weaken). A student who has seen two of these learns to strike the 'has both vs has neither' option on sight and to look for the crossed pair on a weaken stem, which is close to a free solve without reading the mechanism. Roughly half the batch shares that skeleton, so in a form it would be recognisable item to item. (2) The trend-inversion table items (A-06, B-06, C-06) use the same design: one inverted pair is the key, two trend-consistent comparisons, and one distractor that names the inverting site but compares it in the wrong direction. Threshold items (A-04, A-05, C-04, C-05, D-04, D-06) are varied enough, though D-04 sets every distractor at about 0.70, which reads as a tell once one ratio is worked out. Key letters are balanced (A7 B5 C5 D7), so no positional tell. All 24 keys matched my cold answers and every explanation is sound.
